request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Run 2 (LightGBM, all+agent, no imbalance handling) has the best PR-AUC in 5/5 folds against run 1 (random forest) and 4/5 against run 3. Run 3 wins only fold 4 (0.790 vs 0.7765). Run 2 also has the highest mean (0.7328) and the lowest SD (0.056). The edge over run 1 is small but consistent, about 0.01 to 0.04 per fold. Because run 2 beats the simpler random forest in every fold, the extra complexity is justified.

Fold-to-fold spread is large for every run. Fold 3 is the weakest for all three (about 0.60 to 0.65), and the SD of 0.056 is comparable to the gap between runs 1 and 2, so the mean difference is modest. Only 5 folds and 3 configs were tried, so the ranking is not tightly established.

The results look strong for a noisy, undocumented label: ROC-AUC is about 0.945 and precision@50 is about 0.78. This could mean the PotentialFraud label is itself derived from claim patterns, or that the features leak it, for example through volume and size or agent aggregates. Treat the model as ranking suspicion, not detecting confirmed fraud.

The CV scheme is not stated. Claims span 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009, so if folds are random rather than grouped or temporal, optimism is possible. Whether the same provider's data could land in both train and test is also unverified.

The audit queue holds about 100 providers, but precision@50 is the only top-k metric reported, and precision at the actual queue size is unknown. The run 2 agent features (all+agent) add an unexamined dependency that should be checked for leakage before deployment. No further experiment rounds are available.
